cards.a: Name resolution failures: server unreachable, wrong records, TTL/negative cache, or search-domain issues. Verify with nslookup, dig, ping name, and show hosts.

cards.q: What is the DNS resolution flow?
cards.a: Local hosts file, then DNS cache, then query the configured server, then the authoritative server, then the response/cache.

cards.q: What tools isolate DNS resolution from general connectivity?
cards.a: nslookup and dig, which query DNS directly and separate DNS from ping.

cards.q: What does an NXDOMAIN response mean?
cards.a: The name does not exist (no record). It is not the same as the server being down; check the name and record type.

cards.q: What do the A and PTR DNS records map?
cards.a: A maps a name to an IPv4 address (AAAA maps to IPv6). PTR maps an IP address to a name for reverse lookups.

cards.q: What purpose do CNAME, MX, and NS records serve?
cards.a: CNAME is an alias for a name, MX identifies mail servers, and NS identifies nameservers for a domain.

cards.q: What does TTL explain in DNS troubleshooting?
cards.a: Why a stale/old IP persists after a record change, because the TTL is the record lifetime held in caches.

cards.q: What is negative caching in DNS?
cards.a: NXDOMAIN (no record) responses are cached, so a failed lookup can persist even after the record is added.

cards.q: What port does DNS use for queries?
cards.a: UDP 53 for queries, with TCP for large answers.

cards.q: What IOS commands configure the DNS resolver?
cards.a: ip name-server <ip> to set the server, ip domain-lookup to enable resolution, and ip domain-name <suffix> to set the search suffix.

cards.q: A DNS timeout is most likely caused by what?
cards.a: The server being unreachable, often due to a firewall blocking UDP 53.

cards.q: What command shows the IOS DNS cache?
Resolving the wrong host for a name is most likely caused by what?
cards.a: A wrong search domain (ip domain-name) or stale cache/TTL.
